meta.note: Project Hail Mary (Andy Weir, 2021). Realization adjudicated by Opus 5.
meta.provenance: Extraction leaned heavily on one secondary wiki (readifyai.com); the astrophage neutrino/super-cross-sectionality mechanism was independently confirmed against Andy Weir interview coverage before accepting the batch.

items.author: Andy Weir
items.desc: A single-celled space organism that absorbs starlight and stores it as energy, dimming the Sun as it spreads. It keeps a fixed internal temperature of about 96 degrees Celsius whatever its surroundings.

items.author: Andy Weir
items.desc: Astrophage turns absorbed heat energy into mass and back into energy on demand, storing energy at the density of mass-energy equivalence. This is what makes it a compact starship fuel.

items.author: Andy Weir
items.desc: Inside the cell, hydrogen ions collide and their kinetic energy is emitted as pairs of neutrinos. This regulates the cell's temperature and lets it hold energy as mass.

items.author: Andy Weir
items.desc: A property of Astrophage cells that makes them opaque to essentially all radiation and impervious to quantum tunnelling. It makes the organism usable as a radiation shield as well as a fuel.

items.author: Andy Weir
items.desc: A faint infrared arc rising from the Sun's north pole and bending toward Venus. It is the trace of Astrophage migrating between the Sun and Venus.

items.author: Andy Weir
items.desc: A propulsion unit that uses Astrophage as fuel. Infrared light draws the microbes onto a rotating mechanism that cycles through fueling, thrusting and cleaning, and directs their released energy backward as thrust.

items.author: Andy Weir
items.desc: A crewed interstellar ship built around Astrophage fuel and many small spin drives, with a cylindrical crew section, a lab and a rear fuel and propulsion section. It is built for a one-way trip to Tau Ceti.

items.author: Andy Weir
items.desc: Enriched Astrophage is stored in fuel bays and circulated through a thin layer in the ship's hull. The layer also works as radiation shielding.

items.author: Andy Weir
items.desc: The ship splits into crew and fuel-tank halves joined by Zylon cables and spins to produce about one g. This lets standard lab equipment work without redesign for weightlessness.

items.device: Coma pods and automated medical armature
items.author: Andy Weir
items.desc: A medical system that keeps crew in an induced coma through the multi-year voyage. Mechanical arms monitor vitals, feed, clean and treat them, using a fixed procedural algorithm rather than an AI.

items.author: Andy Weir
items.desc: Only a small fraction of people tolerate the long induced coma, so crew are chosen by a specific gene that lets them survive it.

items.author: Andy Weir
items.desc: Unmanned interstellar probes, each with its own spin drive and Astrophage fuel, that accelerate to a large fraction of light speed. They carry data and samples back to Earth.

items.author: Andy Weir
items.desc: A specialised telescope that detects the infrared light Astrophage emits. It finds Astrophage trails, breeding grounds and alien ships, but cannot be used while the spin drive is firing.

items.author: Andy Weir
items.desc: A lab kit for running microbiology experiments on samples in space, used aboard the ship to study Astrophage and related organisms.

items.author: Andy Weir
items.desc: An Eridian material made from pure xenon, normally an unreactive gas. It is very hard, insulating and can be made transparent. It is made by mixing two liquids that set solid.

items.author: Andy Weir
items.desc: A xenonite tube with an airlock built between the human ship and the Eridian ship. It lets two incompatible atmospheres and pressures sit side by side.

items.author: Andy Weir
items.desc: A very long xenonite chain lowered with a probe at its end into a planet's atmosphere to collect samples of organisms. It is strong enough to bear atmospheric drag.

items.author: Andy Weir
items.desc: A single-celled predator that envelops Astrophage and kills it. It naturally holds Astrophage in check at Tau Ceti and dies quickly in the presence of nitrogen.

items.author: Andy Weir
items.desc: A strain of Taumoeba bred by directed evolution in sealed chambers to tolerate nitrogen. It also learns to tunnel through xenonite, escaping containment.

items.author: Andy Weir
items.desc: Eridians are pentagonally symmetrical creatures with mineral carapaces, metallic bones and mercury-based blood. Their muscles run on steam, regulated by two circulatory systems at different temperatures.

items.author: Andy Weir
items.desc: Eridians live in nearly pure ammonia at many times Earth's pressure and around 210 degrees Celsius. A human ship and an Eridian ship therefore need separate sealed environments, and Rocky needs a portable habitat aboard the Hail Mary.

items.author: Andy Weir
items.desc: Eridians have no eyes and perceive the world through sound, building a three-dimensional picture of their surroundings. Rocky can sense the inside of the Hail Mary through its hull.

items.author: Andy Weir
items.desc: The Eridian language is spoken as chords of simultaneous musical notes, each word being a specific combination of notes.

items.author: Andy Weir
items.desc: Waveform analysis software that turns Rocky's chords into English text in real time, so a human and an Eridian can converse.

items.author: Andy Weir
items.desc: A camera Rocky builds that converts light into touch-readable texture, letting a creature with no eyes interpret visual data.
items.details: A head-worn camera rendered as an electrotactile image the user reads by touch.

items.author: Andy Weir
items.desc: The Eridian spaceship that matches the Hail Mary's velocity. Rocky's engine-side workshop is shielded from radiation by surrounding Astrophage fuel.
